```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 3.6)
library(reindeer)
library(dplyr)
has_dsp <- requireNamespace("superassp", quietly = TRUE)
```

reindeer treats an EMU-SDMS speech corpus like a tidy dataset: open it, pull
segments out with a query, measure them, attach speaker data, plot. This
vignette runs that loop on the demo corpus that ships with the package.

```{r open}
corp <- demo_corpus()
corp
```

## Query

`query()` takes an EMU Query Language (EQL) expression and returns a lazy
plan; nothing runs until you use the result.

```{r query}
vowels <- query(corp, "Phonetic == V|@|i:|u:|o:|A:|E|I|O")
vowels            # prints a preview, still lazy
nrow(vowels)      # asking for the size runs the query
```

## Measure

`quantify()` runs a signal-processing routine from **superassp** on every
segment. With `.at = 0.5` you get the value at each segment's midpoint.

```{r quantify, eval = has_dsp}
formants <- quantify(vowels, superassp::trk_formant_forest, .at = 0.5,
                     .use_metadata = FALSE)
formants |>
  select(labels, bundle, F1_Hz, F2_Hz) |>
  head()
```

Measurements are cached per recording, so running the same call again is
nearly instant (see the speaker-aware vignette).

## Add speaker data

Speaker metadata lives in `METADATA.json` files at database, session and
bundle level. Set it once; `biographize()` joins it on.

```{r biographize, eval = has_dsp}
set_metadata(corp, list(Gender = "f", Age = 31), session = "0000")
formants <- biographize(formants)
formants |> select(labels, bundle, Gender, Age) |> head(3)
```

## Plot

```{r plot, eval = has_dsp && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), warning = FALSE}
formants |>
  mutate(F1 = as.numeric(F1_Hz), F2 = as.numeric(F2_Hz)) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(F2, F1, label = labels)) +
  ggplot2::geom_text() +
  ggplot2::scale_x_reverse() + ggplot2::scale_y_reverse() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "F2 (Hz)", y = "F1 (Hz)", title = "Vowel midpoints in the demo corpus")
```

## Speed, caching and parallelism

- Everything runs sequentially unless you ask otherwise: set
  `future::plan(future::multisession)` before `quantify()` and it uses the
  workers; reindeer never changes your plan.
- A corpus is indexed once (`corpus()` on 700 bundles takes a few seconds) and
  re-synced incrementally afterwards, so reopening is about a tenth of a second.
- `quantify()` analyses each bundle's whole file once, slices every segment from
  that, and caches the result per bundle. Repeating a call on the same signals
  takes a fraction of a second; changing the routine, its parameters, a helper
  function it uses, or the audio file invalidates the entry. `clear_cache()`
  empties it.
- Order of magnitude on a laptop: a query takes milliseconds, a cold
  `quantify()` of 250 segments about half a second, `scout()` over 25,000
  segments under a second. The repository's `benchmarking/` directory has the
  measured tables and `tools/bench.R` regenerates them.
